request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[0] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): Hi, this is Priya from Aegis Cloud Security support, I have Sarah on the line with me as well — she's one of our senior engineers on the Protect side. Am I speaking with Yuki?

But starting around, I want to say, last Thursday or Friday, we started seeing backup jobs failing partway through. They initiate, they run for a bit, and then just... stop. No completion, no error that makes a ton of sense.
[4] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Okay, and when you say no error that makes sense — what is the error message actually showing? Like is it a timeout, a permissions thing, or something else?
[5] Yuki Tanaka (customer): It says — let me actually pull it up — it says, uh, 'connector write operation terminated, upstream response code 403.' But here's the thing, the IAM permissions haven't changed. Like, nothing on our CloudPrime side changed that week.
[6] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): Got it, a 403. Yeah that's a good starting point. Sarah, do you want to walk through what that typically maps to in the connector?
[7] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, so a 403 from the S3 connector can actually come from a few different places, it's not always what it looks like on the surface. The first thing I'd want to rule out is whether the IAM role that Aegis Protect is assuming has the right combination of permissions — specifically s3:PutObject, s3:GetBucketLocation, and then also the bucket policy itself. Sometimes people set up the IAM role correctly but the bucket policy has a deny statement that overrides it.
[8] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Okay, so the bucket policy can override the IAM role permissions — yeah, that's a good call, I can check that. We were pretty careful when we set this up but it's possible something got changed on the bucket side.
[9] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Exactly, yeah. And the other thing — do you happen to know if the S3 bucket has any VPC endpoint policies or SCPs at the organization level? Like CloudPrime Service Control Policies? Those can also silently block writes even when IAM looks clean.
[10] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Hmm. SCPs... we do have some org-level policies but I'd have to check with our CloudPrime admin to see if anything changed there. We had a routine policy review around that time actually, now that I think about it.
[11] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): That's actually really useful context, yeah. That timing aligns with when you started seeing the failures, so it's worth checking whether any of those policy changes could have inadvertently restricted the role Aegis is using.
[12] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Yeah, I can loop in our CloudPrime admin after this call. Is there a specific role name or ARN I should reference? I want to make sure they're looking at the right thing.
[13] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yes, so in your Aegis Protect console, if you go to Integrations and then Connector Settings for the S3 connector, you'll see the IAM role ARN that Aegis is using listed under Authentication Details. That's the one your admin should be checking.
[14] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Okay, let me — hold on, I actually have the console open. Integrations... Connector Settings... yeah, okay I see it. The ARN is there, I can copy that out.
[15] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Perfect. And while you're in there, can you also check what region the connector is configured to target? The reason I ask is — we've seen a specific edge case where if the bucket is in one region but the connector config still has the default us-east-1 endpoint, it can cause issues that surface as 403s rather than the more obvious region mismatch error.
[16] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Oh interesting. Uh, the bucket is in us-west-2. And the connector says... endpoint is set to s3.amazonaws.com, no region specified explicitly.
[17] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, so that could actually be a contributing factor. The generic s3.amazonaws.com endpoint will route to us-east-1 by default, and depending on your bucket's config — especially if you have bucket policies that restrict access to specific regions or VPCs — that cross-region request can get blocked.
[18] Yuki Tanaka (customer): So I should change that endpoint to the region-specific one? Like s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com?
[19] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Exactly, yeah, that would be the recommended change. You'd want to update that in the connector settings and then re-test a backup job. It's a pretty quick change to make.
[20] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Okay, that makes sense. And should I do that before or after I check the SCP stuff with the CloudPrime admin? Like what order would you tackle these?
[21] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): I'd actually do the endpoint fix first since you can do that right now without needing anyone else, and then run a test job. If it still fails, then you have a cleaner picture to bring to your CloudPrime admin — you can rule out the endpoint issue and focus the conversation on the policy side.
[22] Yuki Tanaka (customer): That's a good approach, yeah. Okay, I'm going to make that endpoint change now actually, while we're on the call. Bear with me a second.
[23] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Take your time.
[24] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Alright, updated. Saved. So I'll kick off a test backup — it's going to take a few minutes to run. I might not know the result before we hang up but at least I know what to look for.
[25] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): That's totally fine. We'll keep the case open and you can reply directly to the case email with the results. If it still 403s after the endpoint fix, Sarah can pull the connector logs from our side and do a deeper trace.
[26] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yeah, and if you want to share the CloudTrail logs from your CloudPrime account for that time window, that would help a lot too — it'll show exactly what API call was being made and why it was denied.
[27] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Yep, I can pull CloudTrail logs. We have a 30-day retention window so that's no problem. I'll grab the logs from last Thursday through today and attach them to the case.
[28] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): Perfect, that would be really helpful. Okay, so to summarize where we are — you're testing the endpoint fix first, and then pending that result, you'll check with your CloudPrime admin about the SCP policy review and share CloudTrail logs with us. Does that all sound right?
[29] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Yeah, that's the plan. One other thing — is there any way to configure Aegis Protect to retry backup jobs automatically if they fail? Right now it seems like it just stops and I have to manually re-trigger it.
[30] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Yes, there is actually. In the connector settings, under Advanced Options, there's a Retry Policy section — you can configure the number of retry attempts and the backoff interval. It's not enabled by default so it might just be turned off in your config.
[31] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Oh, I didn't even know that was there. I'll look for that when I'm in the settings. That'll help in the meantime even if the root cause isn't fully resolved yet.
[32] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): Yeah, definitely. It won't fix the underlying issue but it should reduce the manual overhead while we sort this out.
[33] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Alright, I think I have enough to work with. I appreciate you both jumping on this — Sarah, the region endpoint thing especially, I wouldn't have caught that on my own.
[34] Sarah Chen (aegis_staff): Happy to help. It's one of those things that trips people up because the error message doesn't point directly at it. Hopefully that's the main culprit.
[35] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): We'll keep an eye on the case and respond as soon as you send over the test results and the CloudTrail logs. Shouldn't be more than a business day turnaround from us.
[36] Yuki Tanaka (customer): Works for me. Thanks again, talk soon.
[37] Priya Patel (aegis_staff): Thanks Yuki, take care.
